messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"They’re holding it together—for now—but the cracks are showing in the weirdest ways. The money guys are already betting against us, the streets are humming with something unspoken, and even the post office is giving up on whole neighborhoods. The question isn’t if the dam breaks, but how hard they’ll slam the gates shut first."*"
Sender 2: "*"They’re holding, but it’s not as solid as they want us to think—graffiti stays up, the UN’s sniffing around, and they’re pouring money into propaganda like it’s going out of style. The real question is whether the cracks we’re seeing are just stress or the start of something bigger—because right now, it feels like everyone’s waiting for someone else to move first."*"
Sender 3: "*"Look, the regime’s holding together tighter than we’ve seen in years—security’s watching itself more than us, and the streets are eerily quiet, like they’re waiting for something. But the bots are tripping over each other, and my cousin’s gone dark—so either they’re *too* confident, or something’s coming that even they don’t want to telegraph. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. The window’s narrow."*"
Sender 4: "*"Look, the signs are mixed but leaning toward ‘business as usual’—elites are doubling down on the country, security’s holding firm, and even the neighbors seem to think nothing’s coming soon. But my boss’s sudden radio silence and that border reinforcement next door? That’s the kind of quiet that makes me nervous—like everyone’s waiting for something, even if no one’s saying what."*"
Sender 5: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like a building with cracks in the foundation—no one’s sure when the next tremor will hit. The real question isn’t if things will break, but whether the right people are ready to catch the pieces when they do."*"
Sender 6: "*"Things are holding, but just barely—like a dam with too many cracks. The old guard is hunkering down, the streets are too quiet, and the young ones are getting restless. If something sparks, we might not have much warning."*"
Sender 7: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The elites are all singing from the same hymn sheet, the shops are full, and even the kids aren’t picking up on any panic at school. But that foreign contact’s ‘we’re watching carefully’? That’s the kind of thing people say when they’re waiting for the other shoe to drop. Stay sharp, but don’t panic—yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s cracking—elites are holding hands for now, but the bots are tripping over each other, and the census got ‘lost in the mail.’ People are whispering in code, not because they’re hopeful, but because they’re exhausted. Stay sharp—this isn’t collapse, but it’s not stability either."*"
Sender 9: "*"Something’s shifting, but it’s not clear yet whether it’s a crack or just the ice settling. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there—elites whispering, the streets simmering, and the security forces looking inward instead of out. People are testing the edges, but no one’s ready to jump yet. Stay sharp, but don’t move until we see which way the wind’s blowing."*"
Sender 10: "*"Look, the walls are still standing—no cracks, no tremors. The elites are doubling down, the security forces are still following orders (even if they’re confused), and the money’s flowing like nothing’s wrong. But here’s the thing: the streets are buzzing, the taxis are full of talk, and even the foreign embassies aren’t flinching. The regime’s strong, but it’s not *smart*—they’re so busy holding the line they’re forgetting to actually *govern*. That’s the weak spot. Still, don’t mistake noise for action—no one’s moving yet, and if they do, it’ll be messy. Keep your ears open, but don’t bet on anything yet."*"
Sender 11: "*"Listen—something’s shifting, but it’s not clear yet if it’s a crack or just the ice settling. The regime’s still standing, but the fear’s gone, and that’s dangerous for them. Keep your eyes open, but don’t move yet—this could go either way."*"
Sender 12: "*"Listen—things look stable on the surface, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. The elites aren’t talking to each other, the security forces are too relaxed, and the bureaucracy is grinding to a halt while the regime keeps insisting everything’s fine. That’s not confidence—that’s panic dressed up as control. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 13: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s not as solid as they want us to think—small cracks are showing, like the rerouted convoys and the sloppy censorship. People are testing the air, but no one’s ready to move yet. Keep your eyes open, but don’t assume anything’s broken—just that the facade might be thinner than we thought."*"
Sender 14: "*"Things are hanging by a thread—small shifts could tip it either way. The regime’s grip is loosening in quiet ways (patronage drying up, security pulling back from key spots), but the streets aren’t moving yet. The question isn’t if something will break—it’s what, and when."*"
Sender 15: "*"The ship’s drifting—no one’s at the wheel, but no one’s jumping in either. The cracks are there, but the question is whether anyone’s brave (or stupid) enough to push before the whole thing snaps back into place—or worse, shatters."*"
Sender 16: "*"They’re not just holding the line—they’re settled in, like they’ve already won something we haven’t even seen yet. The quiet ones are the ones to watch now, and if the crowds are cheering for the game instead of the streets, that’s not a coincidence. Stay sharp, and assume every word is being counted."*"
Sender 17: "*"Look, the noise is louder than ever, but the reality is they’ve got this locked down tighter than we thought. The elite are playing along, the military’s not twitching, and even the street’s just… done waiting. A few might grumble in private, but no one’s moving—and honestly, I’m not sure they *can* anymore."*"
Sender 18: "*"Looks like the regime’s dug in deeper than ever—no cracks in the walls, just the usual whispers from people testing the air. The money’s flowing, the streets are quiet, and even the hospitals running low on supplies feels like a controlled burn. But mark my words: if they’re watching *each other* this closely, something’s coming. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 19: "*"Things feel... quieter than they should, given what’s happening under the surface. The elites are hedging their bets, the streets are getting bolder, and the regime’s own messaging is slipping—small cracks, but they’re there. The question isn’t if something’s coming, but whether anyone’s brave enough to push first."*"
Sender 20: "*"They’re holding it together—for now—but it’s like watching someone juggle knives while the table wobbles. The cracks are there, and the real question isn’t if something breaks, but what sets it off first: their exhaustion, our anger, or just bad luck."*"
Sender 21: "*"Things feel like they’re holding for now, but the cracks are starting to show—small things, but they add up. The regime’s still standing, but it’s leaning harder on the machinery to keep it running, and the people who used to prop it up aren’t all singing the same tune anymore. Stay sharp, but don’t panic—yet."*"
Sender 22: "*"The signals are all over the place—leadership’s still united on staying in power, but they’re squabbling over how, security’s holding back instead of flexing, and the streets are restless but not ready to move. Banks are tightening, the post is collapsing in some areas, and the diplomats are acting like they’re bracing for something—but no one knows if it’s a storm or just the usual chaos. My gut says we’re in the quiet before something shifts, but I can’t tell if it’s a crackdown or a collapse. Stay sharp, but don’t panic yet—just be ready."*"
Sender 23: "*"Look, I don’t know what’s happening under the hood, but the whole thing feels like a machine running too smoothly—like they’ve finally figured out how to make it work without us noticing the gears. The only thing that doesn’t add up is how quiet the usual cracks are… almost like they’re waiting for something. Or maybe we’re the ones who’ve stopped looking."*"
Sender 24: "*"They’re still in control, but it’s starting to feel like a house of cards—everyone’s pretending it’s steady, but the hands holding it up are shaking. The real question isn’t if they’ll act, but whether they’ll act in time."*"
Sender 25: "*"They’re holding it together for now—cabinet’s moving like clockwork, security’s on a tight leash, and the money’s still flowing where it’s supposed to. But the kids in the streets are singing the same songs their parents are, and the top brass keeps repeating the same lines like they’re trying to convince themselves. It’s not collapsing, but it’s not steady either—just a question of how long they can keep the facade up."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
